system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Every prompt has two parts: the “system prompt” (see more details in Appendix A.3) and the “agent prompt.”
system_prompt_style.note: System prompt files under data/prompts/system/ selected by PromptSettings.main_prompt config.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: In both Lean and Coq, we instantiate the retrieval mechanism to be a BM25 search.
env_context_strategy.note: Default EvalSettings has use_example_retrieval: bool = False; env_settings include bm25_retrieval.yaml configs.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: It also includes logic for trimming this information to fit the most relevant parts in the LLM’s context window.
context_compaction.note: max_history_messages: int = 0 in EvalSettings (src/copra/main/config.py) bounds retained history.

observation_format.evidence_quote: The feedback from the execution is used to construct a new prompt for the policy, and the process repeats.

tool_call_format.note: Grammar-parsed tag-delimited actions ([RUN TACTIC]...[END]); closest value is xml_tags.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: The actions in our MDP are the proof environment’s tactics.
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing tool; actions are proof tactics.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: The system prompt describes the rules of engagement for the LLM. It contains a grammar (distinct from the one for agent prompts) that we expect the LLMs to follow

protocol_standardization.note: No MCP/A2A mentioned anywhere in README, file tree or paper.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The COPRA agent solves the theorem-proving problem via a GPT-4-directed depth-first search over tactic sequences.
loop_primitives.note: DFS with backtracking (tree_search) is default policy PolicyName.Dfs; tactic executed and error feedback fed back.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: At each time step, it prompts the LLM to select the next tactic to apply.
planning_granularity.note: No stored plan object; optional informal proof can serve as global context.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: a wrapper around a pretrained LLM (GPT-4) that can learn in-context — and show that this policy can achieve a high reward. It is this policy that defines ourlanguage agent.

delegation_mechanism.note: Single policy driven by ProofAgent; no delegation code.

human_in_loop.note: src/copra/agent/human_policy.py exists as a human-as-policy substitute, not approval gating.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: the algorithm maintains a stack of environment states and a “failure dictionary” Bad that maps states to sets of tactics that are known to be “unproductive” at the state.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Since COPRA relies on a black-box LLM, we do not perform any training with the train set, but do use it as the retrieval database for our Coq experiments.
long_term_memory.note: Static lemma retrieval DB is not cross-run agent memory.

state_persistence.note: should_checkpoint: bool = False by default; EvalRunCheckpointInfo records per-theorem success to skip/resume evaluation runs.

self_verification.note: Harness compiles/validates the found proof in the ITP and retries if validation fails; closest value to proof-checker execution.

rollback.note: Search-level backtracking over proof states exists, but no file/repo rollback mechanism.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: while not done and not stop_policy(steps, additional_info):
termination_condition.note: max_steps_per_episode: int = 50 and max_number_of_episodes cap steps; EXIT action from policy is model_declared; timeout_in_secs also ends runs; progress check rejects non-progress states.

cost_controls.note: Also max_history_messages limits prompt size; no caching/routing found.

timeouts.note: timeout_per_theorem_in_secs: int = 720 in EvalBenchmark is the per-run limit.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: Services (PISA, Llama) are automatically managed by COPRA
execution_isolation.note: ITP REPL/services run locally on the host; no container isolation documented.

filesystem_access.note: Agent actions are tactics applied within a given ITP project; no general filesystem tool.

network_policy.evidence_quote: # vLLM server starts automatically on port 48000 (override with VLLM_PORT)
network_policy.note: No network restriction configuration present; LLM API calls go out freely.

permission_model.evidence_quote: state, modified_action, next_state, reward, done, info = env.step(action)
permission_model.note: Parsed tactics are executed directly in the ITP with no authorization layer.

tracing.note: proof_dump_dir default ".log/proofs/proof-dump-"; EvalProofResults stores ProofSearchResult JSON; logging also present.

replayability.evidence_quote: In our experiments, we set the “temperature” parameter to zero to ensure the LLM outputs are as deterministic as possible.
replayability.note: Proof dumps record trajectories; no replay runner cited.

guardrails.note: Progress check and failure dictionary block unproductive/erroneous tactics.

target_domain.evidence_quote: COPRA: An in-COntext PRoof Agent which uses LLMs like GPTs to prove theorems in formal languages.
target_domain.note: Domain is formal theorem proving; closest allowed value is other (math/formal proof).

open_source.evidence_quote: Our code and data are available at https://github.com/trishullab/copra.
open_source.note: No LICENSE file visible in the listed file tree; PyPI package published.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Our implementation of COPRA is LLM-agnostic, and functions as long as the underlying language model is capable of producing responses which parse according to the output grammar.

primary_artifact.note: Pinned repo state (Lean 4, vLLM, simple CLI) postdates the 2024 paper.
